newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Thai refiners commit excess gasoline in term deals.
newsitem.headline: Thai refiners commit excess gasoline in term deals.

text.p: Two Thai refiners have committed their excess gasoline cargoes in term contracts, industry sources said on Thursday.
The start up of two new refineries this year has boosted total refining capacity by 275,000 barrels-per-day to 860,000 bpd and turned Thailand into an exporter of gasoline since July.
"All the barrels have been termed out to a few companies on one to two year contracts," said a source from Caltex, the joint venture between U.S. majors Texaco Inc and Chevron Inc.
"But due to a confidentiality clause, we cannot give further details."

Industry sources, however, said Star Refinery, a joint venture between Caltex and state-owned Petroleum Authority of Thailand (PTT), has concluded at least one two-year term contract to sell one 170,000-barrel (20,000-tonne) cargo a month at a 95 cent discount per barrel to Singapore spot quotes.
The price is on a free-on-board (fob) basis from Star's 130,000 barrel-per-day (bpd) refinery at rayong.
Star started spot exports of gasoline when the new refinery began commercial production in the middle of the year.
The sources said Thai Oil, the other refiner which has exported spot cargoes, also has committed its excess barrels, but on a shorter six-month term contract.
Thai Oil started to export one to two 250,000 barrel-cargoes a month in July from its 220,000 bpd refinery at Sri Racha.
The sources said in spite of having commissioned its 145,0000 bpd Rayong refinery in January, Royal Dutch/Shell Group would not start exporting until the end of the year.
They said independent traders with storage in Australia had been moving cargoes from Thailand.
